chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:

The wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, used to leave the yellow trace of perfume on their bodies when they performed ghusl from janabah, and that was because the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, instructed them to pour water thoroughly over their bodies.

key_terms.أَجْسَادِهِنَّ: their bodies, over which the water was to be poured
key_terms.اغْتَسَلْنَ: they performed ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.الطِّيبِ: perfume or scented substance applied to the body
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.صُفْرَةَ: the yellow trace or coloration remaining

ai.seo_question: Does the remaining trace of perfume on the body affect the validity of ghusl from janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله regarding ghusl from janabah. It indicates that the remaining color of perfume on the body did not prevent the validity of the ghusl, so long as water was poured over the body properly.
